propositions: A context-limit escalation on a Bedrock-qualified run silently relocates the call to direct Anthropic by bypassing the model-class vocabulary and using a bare model id inferred from MODEL_LADDER constants

The _rung_target function compares only the rung's provider-inferred form against class resolution, never consulting the actual run's model, causing provider-qualified primaries to degrade to unqualified targets
Pass-1 entry rung uses frontier model which resolves to bare anthropic id, triggering unintended substitution on common one-criterion retry before any escalation is needed

When no model-class table is configured and cfg.model is provider-qualified, the Bedrock ladder is not consulted, causing escalation to cross provider boundaries and create invalid model ids like bedrock:claude-opus-4-8

_rung_target must receive the run's primary model as input and apply a provider-agreement rule: if target provider differs from primary provider on a higher rung, drop the rung rather than crossing providers
The fix preserves back-compat byte-for-byte for unqualified or Anthropic-qualified primaries while preventing silent provider jumps and unnameable rung escalations that exceed the class vocabulary
